title: The Head Count
hook: At the lake camp, the rule for the midnight swim was simple: count them going in, count them coming out.
lines: The summer I was nineteen, I ran the midnight swim at a lake camp.
There was one rule. Count them going in. Count them coming out. And if the numbers don't match... don't go looking.
All summer, it was easy. Twelve kids in. Twelve kids out.
Then came the last night of August. No wind. The lake was flat and black, like glass.
Twelve went in. I counted twice.
When I blew the whistle, they waded back up the beach, laughing and shivering.
I counted again. Thirteen dripping kids in towels... and every one of them was smiling at me.
So I did what the rule said. I didn't look closer. I walked them to the cabins and locked the door.
All night, I heard small wet footsteps, walking circles around the cabin.
In the morning, I told the director we had an extra camper.
She looked at her clipboard. Then at me. Very slowly.
Honey... we've only had eleven campers all summer.
